Solutions 1 and 3 both give $K_c = 2/m$ for $m \ge 2$. Solution 2 gives $K_c = 1$, which cannot be right because the problem asks for a function of $m$.

I checked the mode-$k$ linearization, which uses the sine-type convention in which the Kuramoto model has its standard threshold. The uniform state's $k$-th mode has growth rate proportional to $\tfrac{K c_k k}{2} - Dk^2$, so the threshold is $K_c^{(k)} = 2Dk/c_k$. Normalizing so that $K_c = 1$ at $m=0$ gives $D = 1/2$. Then the first harmonic gives $K_c^{(1)} = 1$ and the second gives $K_c^{(2)} = 2/m$. The second harmonic destabilizes first exactly when $2/m < 1$, i.e. $m > 2$. For $m \ge 2$, the transition is then $K_c = 2/m$.

Solution 1 derives this cleanly. Solution 3 reaches the same answer, but its final line is garbled ("(2/m)*m >= 2"), so Solution 1 is the cleaner choice.

I did not verify that the mode-2 bifurcation is continuous when the first harmonic is also present, so the result rests on the linear-instability argument.

CHOICE: 1
